said artificial intelligence companies concerned about the safety of their own technology can slow or stop development themselves.
In an interview on "Fox News Sunday" published Sunday, Kratsios said companies that believe they are developing unsafe technology do not need the government to force them to pause.
"If you do believe that you’re developing a technology that is unsafe or you don’t want it out in the world, you can just stop it," Kratsios said. "You don’t need someone to force you to do that."

"There’s leaders of these companies that are going out and saying, we’re going to do all these measures, the government has to do all these things, when in reality, they just need to slow down if they feel that they need to do so," he said.
Kratsios said AI regulation should be "use case and sector specific," pointing to different agencies overseeing applications involving drones, self-driving cars and medical diagnostics.
He also criticized broad, "one size fits all" approaches to AI regulation.
